findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new OR branch in deleteMany deletes any SMS WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, so the scheduledDate condition no longer bounds deletion. A reminder that failed twice (retryCount=2) but whose scheduled date is still days in the future is permanently deleted on the next cron run, so that recipient never receives any SMS — the retry cap silently becomes a hard drop even when there was ample time to retry later. Anyone running overlapping deployments or frequent cron invocations gets bitten.

[ADVISORY] The retryCount increment reads the stale value fetched before the loop (reminder.retryCount + 1) rather than using an atomic increment ({ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }), so concurrent runs perform lost updates. Two overlapping cron executions (common with deploy overlap or manual re-trigger) both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, so a reminder can be attempted far more than the intended 2 times — extra Twilio sends and cost — while the deleteMany gate undercounts attempts.

[ADVISORY] The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block is itself unguarded, so if it throws (e.g., P2025 because the row was concurrently deleted by another run's deleteMany) the rejection escapes the catch that was supposed to make the loop resilient. A single failed bookkeeping update aborts the whole for-loop, skipping every remaining reminder in that run; the operator sees only a generic error and reminders silently stop being scheduled for that cycle.

[ADVISORY] The type cast to (PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[] papers over the fact that the upstream reminders fetch has no retryCount-based filter, and the cast will silently hide future schema drift between the Prisma select and the hand-maintained type intersection. The next developer adding a field to the select must remember to extend this parallel type union; if they rely on the cast instead of updating PartialWorkflowReminder, TypeScript keeps compiling with runtime fields the type denies — a maintenance trap for whoever extends this endpoint next.

[BUG] The new `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` delete branch has no `method` filter, so it deletes non-SMS WorkflowReminders (EMAIL, etc.) whose retryCount exceeds 1. If any other code path ever writes retryCount, the SMS cron hard-deletes email reminders; the original query carefully scoped to WorkflowMethods.SMS but the sibling flag (method) was silently dropped on the new OR branch.

[BUG] The retryCount>1 deletion is unconditional on scheduledDate, so a reminder whose scheduledDate is in the future (within the 7-day scheduling window) is hard-deleted after two failed attempts. A transient Twilio failure twice in a row causes the reminder to be permanently deleted instead of retried or marked failed — the user never gets the SMS and the record is gone, losing audit state; the original query only deleted past-dated reminders.

[BUG] Retry count is incremented but never checked before attempting to schedule, so the cap is only enforced by the destructive deleteMany at the start of the next cron run. The acceptance criterion 'stop retrying after N attempts' is implemented as 'send, then delete the row afterwards' rather than 'check retryCount <= max before sending'; behavior depends on cron timing, and there is no constant defining the max retry, making the policy of '2 attempts' an unverified implicit invariant buried in a SQL comparison.

[ADVISORY] The catch-block retry increment and the else-branch retry increment are duplicated hand-maintained blocks of identical logic. The next change to retry policy (e.g., also setting a failedAt timestamp or capping) must be applied in two places and will drift; extraction to a single incrementReminderRetry(reminder.id) helper deletes one of the blocks.

[ADVISORY] No tests anywhere in the diff cover the new retry-count lifecycle (increment on failure, delete at retryCount>1, method-scoped deletion); the diff contains no test-shaped files (no *.spec.*, *.test.*, spec/**, test/** matches) touching this handler. A regression in the deleteMany OR-clause (e.g., the missing method filter already present here) would silently delete reminder rows in production with no verification step catching it.

[BUG] The deleteMany OR-branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method, silently destroying EMAIL and other-channel reminders. Once a reminder of any method hits retryCount 2, the next cron run hard-deletes it, so email/other-channel reminders stop being sent and bookings lose those reminders entirely — no cancellation event, no audit; the stated intent (SMS retry count tracking) does not authorize deleting non-SMS rows.

[BUG] The retry cap is implemented as a destructive delete of the reminder row rather than exclusion from scheduling, so a reminder that exhausts retries is removed from the database instead of being marked failed/expired. The booking loses the reminder record (including its bookingUid index linkage and any partial scheduling state) permanently; the requirement traceable to 'retry count tracking' is tracking, not deletion — this is implementation work not traceable to the stated intent and destroys data while doing it.

[BUG] The else branch increments retryCount on the non-scheduling path (when a scheduled SMS was found), so a reminder that is already successfully scheduled gets its retry counter incremented each cron run and is then deleted by the deleteMany retryCount > 1 clause. An already-scheduled SMS reminder is re-fetched every run (the findMany has no retryCount/scheduled filter shown), its retryCount climbs by 1 per run, and after 3 cron runs the deleteMany branch removes it from the DB — successfully scheduled reminders self-destruct, breaking the retry invariant the PR claims to enforce.

[ADVISORY] The findMany that selects unscheduled reminders has no retryCount filter, so exhausted reminders are only excluded via the preceding destructive deleteMany rather than by a query predicate. The retry cap enforcement is coupled to row deletion; a future refactor or a failed delete leaves uncapped reminders re-scheduled forever, and the intent 'limit retries' is not enforced by any invariant on the read path.

[ADVISORY] Retry-count mutation logic (increment by 1 from a stale in-memory value) is duplicated in two places (else branch and catch block). Any change to retry semantics (e.g., max attempts, backoff) must be edited in two sites; the observed pattern invites drift, and a future editor updating one site silently leaves the other on old behavior.

[BUG] The new OR branch in deleteMany drops the method and scheduledDate filters, deleting any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or scheduled date. A reminder that failed scheduling twice is silently and permanently deleted on the next run — it never sends and leaves no record; the deletion also applies to future-scheduled rows and would delete non-SMS reminders if any other path ever increments retryCount. Users simply stop receiving reminders with no failure state, since the delete fires unconditionally at the top of every invocation.

[ADVISORY] The retry cap is enforced by a cross-run side effect: the increment path writes retryCount here while a different query (the deleteMany at the top of the NEXT invocation) is what actually stops retries, coupling two code sites to implement one state machine. The next editor who touches the deleteMany where-clause or the increment logic independently will break retry termination (either infinite retries or premature deletion); a reminder can also be retried once more than intended because the delete only happens on a subsequent cron run after retryCount already exceeds 1.

[ADVISORY] retryCount is incremented from the stale in-memory value (reminder.retryCount + 1) rather than an atomic increment, in a cron handler that can run concurrently with itself. Two overlapping invocations of this endpoint read the same retryCount and each write the same +1, undercounting actual retry attempts and delaying the cap by one extra round of API calls to Twilio per reminder per race.

[BUG] The new deleteMany OR clause drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter for the retryCount > 1 branch, so the cleanup deletes reminders of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1 — and any future code path (or manual data fix) that writes retryCount on an EMAIL reminder will cause this handler to silently delete that email reminder even though its scheduledDate is still in the future. Non-SMS reminders with retryCount > 1 are permanently deleted by what was originally an SMS-only past-due cleanup, and their scheduledDate-in-future guard is bypassed entirely for that branch — the handler now deletes reminders that are not yet due, which the original deleteMany explicitly guarded against with the scheduledDate lte check.

[ADVISORY] The catch-path increments retryCount unconditionally, including for non-recoverable errors (invalid phone number, Twilio auth failure, malformed booking payload), so all failures are treated as retryable and the reminder is deleted after two attempts with no log distinguishing exhausted-retries from other deletions. Operators debugging why a reminder vanished will find only the generic 'Error scheduling SMS' console.log and no record of the deleted reminder; users with permanently invalid numbers consume two Twilio call attempts per reminder before silent deletion, and there is no observability that the give-up threshold was hit.

[ADVISORY] The else branch increments retryCount whenever scheduledSMS.sid is falsy, which conflates 'Twilio returned a message with no sid' (a send whose outcome is unknown) with a definitive failure, changing the prior behavior of leaving the reminder untouched in that case. A reminder whose message object lacks a sid is now counted as a retry twice and then deleted, where previously it would be re-attempted indefinitely — a silent behavior change to the send-outcome contract that the PR description (retry count tracking) does not state.

[BUG] The new OR clause `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` in the deleteMany where filter has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, so reminders of every method (email, SMS, etc.) with retryCount > 1 are permanently deleted by this endpoint. Any workflow reminder whose retry count exceeds 1 — including non-SMS reminders owned by other booking workflows — is hard-deleted whenever this schedule endpoint runs, silently destroying pending reminders for bookings; no audit trail, no ownership scoping beyond the retry counter itself.

[ADVISORY] The catch block interpolates the raw error object into a log line via `console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`)`, which can include Twilio API response details and payload contents in server logs (pre-existing line, but the diff adds a new error-producing failure path around it with no redaction). Operators tailing logs may capture Twilio request/response metadata including phone numbers and account identifiers for the newly-added retryCount update failure path; low security impact but worth a structured, redacted logger.

[ADVISORY] The new OR-branch deletes reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, but the retry cap semantics are self-inconsistent: increments only ever reach 2 via the two increment sites, so a reminder gets exactly one retry and is then hard-deleted before a second retry, and the deleteMany also wipes future-scheduled reminders once retryCount hits 2. Operators relying on this cron to actually retry failed SMS reminders see reminders vanish after a single retry, and reminders deleted via the retryCount>1 predicate are removed even while still scheduled in Twilio, leaving orphaned scheduled SMS that will fire with no corresponding WorkflowReminder row. No test in this diff exercises the deleteMany OR predicate, the retryCount increment on the error path, or the else-branch increment, so none of this is verified.

[ADVISORY] The else branch (scheduledSMS lookup returned null) increments retryCount unconditionally, conflating 'Twilio listSMS call returned no matching scheduled SMS' with 'sending failed', including the case where the reminder was simply cancelled or already processed between queries. Reminders that are legitimately absent from the Twilio response get their retryCount incremented toward the deleteMany threshold, and a race between the findMany and the listSMS call can cause a valid reminder to be deleted after two cron runs. No test distinguishes the else-branch from the catch-branch, and neither new increment path nor the new deleteMany predicate has any test coverage in this diff (no test-shaped files changed at all — verified by scanning the diff).

[BUG] The new OR branch in deleteMany drops the method filter, so ANY WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 — regardless of method (SMS/email/calendar) and regardless of scheduledDate — is unconditionally deleted. The retryCount condition is not scoped under method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, so if any other reminder type ever gets retryCount incremented (or a future writer touches the shared column), this handler silently destroys those rows, including future-dated non-SMS reminders; the delete also ignores scheduledDate, so an SMS reminder with retryCount > 1 that is scheduled in the future is deleted mid-deploy-window.

[ADVISORY] Both new update sites write retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 from the value read at query time (line ~53), so concurrent invocations of this handler perform lost updates. Two overlapping cron/manual runs both read retryCount=0, both write 1, so a reminder that failed twice only counts one retry; the retry-limit deletion (retryCount > 1) then under-fires and failed reminders retry more times than intended, sending duplicate SMS to attendees.

[ADVISORY] The else branch increments retryCount when the reminder was already scheduled (the success-but-already-scheduled path), so successfully scheduled reminders accumulate retry counts and are then destroyed by the retryCount > 1 deleteMany on a subsequent run. A reminder that succeeds via the 'already scheduled' branch twice is silently deleted with its booking reference, cancelling SMS reminders that were correctly in place — data loss with no backup/export step.

[BUG] When the Twilio call resolves but returns a falsy scheduledSMS/sid, the handler increments retryCount and moves on, so after two such outcomes the reminder is silently deleted by the next run's deleteMany without an SMS ever being sent. A booking owner who opted into SMS reminders gets no reminder and no error anywhere — the API returns { ok: true } while the reminder record is eventually destroyed via the retryCount > 1 delete clause; the only trace is the record vanishing. Users miss bookings with no signal to operators.

[BUG] The new deleteMany OR clause matches retryCount > 1 with no method filter and no scheduledDate bound, so it deletes future-dated WorkflowReminder rows of any method that happen to carry retryCount > 1, including ones scheduled to send later. Any reminder row (SMS or otherwise) whose retryCount exceeds 1 is permanently deleted even if its scheduledDate is days in the future, silently cancelling reminders that were still pending; once other code paths start writing retryCount (e.g. an email retry tracker), this clause destroys their state too.

[BUG] The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block is itself unguarded, so a DB failure (or a reminder deleted concurrently by the deleteMany of a parallel invocation) throws out of the per-reminder try/catch and aborts the whole handler loop with an unhandled error. The exception propagates past the loop with no response sent, remaining reminders in this run are never scheduled, and the endpoint surfaces as a raw 500 instead of the JSON contract the success path returns — one transient Prisma error in the error path takes down the entire batch.

[ADVISORY] The retry accounting is computed from the in-memory reminder.retryCount snapshot rather than an atomic increment (data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }), so two overlapping invocations of this endpoint read the same retryCount and both write the same +1 value. Concurrent cron/manual invocations under-count retries: a reminder that failed four times can still show retryCount 1 or 2 and keep being retried (or, racing with deleteMany, be deleted mid-iteration causing the update in the catch block to throw on a missing record).

This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

This matches the finding’s core concern about unbounded deletion and potential permanent drop of future reminders after two failures, and it contradicts the nearby comment about only deleting past-due scheduled SMS reminders.

If that update throws (e.g., record missing due to concurrent deletion such as the earlier `deleteMany` OR another run), the exception will escape the catch and can abort processing of subsequent reminders in the loop. The diff shows no nested try/catch or fallback around that bookkeeping update.
